subject.title: refactor(memory): drop redundant agent-id scoping from qmd collection names

question: Should OpenClaw replace the shipped agent-scoped QMD collection identifiers with unscoped per-index identifiers and run a one-time scoped-to-unscoped rebuild migration?
rationale: Source and upstream contracts show that the change is feasible and well implemented, but they cannot establish whether the shipped suffix is intentionally reserved for future shared-index semantics; the canonical issue explicitly leaves that policy choice to maintainers.

options.title: Adopt unscoped names
options.body: Make each agent's isolated QMD index the sole namespace boundary and accept the one-time derived-index rebuild on upgrade.

options.title: Keep scoped names
options.body: Preserve the shipped suffix and close the proposal if future shared-index semantics or stable operational identifiers outweigh the simplification.

recommendation.title: Adopt unscoped names
recommendation.body: Make each agent's isolated QMD index the sole namespace boundary and accept the one-time derived-index rebuild on upgrade.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the major memory host and plugin ownership refactors and is the strongest available history-backed owner for this architecture choice.
